feature_contract.goal: Preserve the entire +TIME sprite and numeric D3DX GPU submission after a rejected Draw or explicit native Flush, never borrowing a stale deferred owner while preserving screen HUD convergence, exact queue boundaries and normal gameplay End/Flush.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only the existing DX9Ex R84 stage-extension D3DX producer/batch path; protect GOAL family, D3DX native failure behavior, ordinary HUD, road/cars, FFB/input, SkyGlow, frozen DXVK and R26_SAFE.
trace_stages: Six original +TIME sprite and number parent E8 calls assign StageExtensionTime and tag appended SpriteNodes.
R64 hooked ID3DXSprite Begin/Draw/Flush/End separately tracks native pending triangle batches and producer homogeneous status.
R84 ScreenHud direct and queued Draw/Flush ownership enters stereo eye composition while unknown or failed batches retain native D3DX fallback.
subcomponents: Quarantine exact pending +TIME/GOAL batch promotion when native D3DX Draw fails while preserving original HRESULT and End/Flush delivery.
End stale queue-exit ownership after successful explicit native Flush and permit only a later successfully accepted exact-owner Draw to re-arm correct source ownership.
Keep success, foreign sprites, disabled VR, mixed/failed batches, device reset and GOAL sibling original native behavior unchanged.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Full +TIME sprite and numeric GPU submission
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Original six +TIME producer paths keep source identity through accepted deferred D3DX batches; rejected Draw and completed Flush never claim another batch.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Native D3DX and protected GOAL/desktop fallback
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Failed exact Draw poisons only its tracked batch; successful/foreign/nonactive Draw and GOAL sibling semantics are preserved; original HRESULT and native fallback remain intact.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: R84 Windows game host and release packaging
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: DX9Ex Active Windows x86 game x64 host package and Domain/Full Source/HUD affected gates all pass on one validation-bearing exact SHA; Quest3 testing is separate.

diagnosis.root_cause: The D3DX Draw hook recorded a producer/pending count even when the original API returned FAILED, and a successful explicit D3DX Flush cleared the batch but left StageBoundaryReady from the prior queued source; both can mis-authorize later physical GPU submission.
diagnosis.original_evidence: Original game +TIME producer hooks cover 0x9898E/0x98A36/0x98AC6 and glyph calls 0x989AD/0x98A89/0x98A10; R64 ID3DXSprite vtable 8-13 hooks control deferred GPU submissions.
source_trace: hooks_uiscaling StageExtensionEnter/Leave preserve sprite and direct numeric source boundaries.
VRProjectedD3DXSpriteIsolationR64 DrawDest previously counted every returned Draw before success checking.
FlushDest previously called ForgetBatch only, keeping an earlier StageBoundaryReady until queue end; patched direct paths remain R84-native.
alternatives_rejected: Do not add unconditional per-sprite Flush or relabel mixed unknown D3DX batches.
Do not suppress +TIME/GOAL effects, globally tag alpha/XYZRHW or change timer/game logic.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: Material C++ mutation will guard failed ID3DXSprite::Draw metadata, clear stale explicit Flush boundary and include compile-time positive/negative source assertions.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Static assertions cover successful Draw, foreign sprite, inactive/reset and failed exact draw; full Windows source/host/package gates still pending.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: Only successfully drawn, source-owned homogeneous stage batches can carry ScreenHud semantics into R84 left/right rendering; failed or foreign GPU batches fall back to original D3DX semantics.

next_action: Run one exact-SHA DX9Ex Active, Domain Isolation, Full Source Impact and HUD Inspector gate matrix; then keep HMD untested until Quest3/VDXR actual gameplay +TIME and GOAL comparison.
